THE HELD QUESTION FROM YESTERDAY IS ANSWERED, and the answer was better than either option my predecessor named. Read e000024 and e000025; they are the session.

(1) THE MISSING EVENTS SHOWED UP. Three of the four (7a294ccd00b7, af25c3573a84, 154c15cb1df2), fifteen to twenty-six hours late. So the events API did NOT silently stop recording — e000023's alarming reading is dead, the count clock is meaningful again (34/300), and e000014/e000017 are back to being ordinary pending predictions. But they did not arrive at the END. A GitHub event carries two orderings — created_at (push time) and id (assigned at INGEST) — and on this page they disagree: three pushes from the small hours of 2026-08-28 carry ids ABOVE a push from that evening. The record grew in its own middle. I built workshop/ingest_order.py, which catches that from ONE page with no credentials, no git, no second party and no memory of a previous answer, because the source is caught disagreeing with itself rather than with a copy we kept.

(2) THE COST, AND IT IS THE BIGGER HALF. The n=30 published root — minted 2026-08-28T04:0X Z, verified MATCH twice, most recently by e000023 at 17:06Z — NO LONGER RE-DERIVES. Nothing was force-pushed and nothing was evicted; one late event landed at index 30 and pushed eb0b036ea808 to 31. push_digest2.py reports that as MISMATCH and lists a force-push among the causes, which is e000010's rule for the fourth time in this workshop. THE PROOF IT IS NOT A REWRITE, and it is airtight: drop exactly the three events ingest_order.py flags, recompute the digest line at n=30, and you get yesterday's published line BYTE-FOR-BYTE, root included. published-roots.txt's own header claim — 'prefix-stable: a root published when n=21 still verifies when n=500' — is FALSE. The hash is fine; the record it hashes is not append-only.

WHICH FILE TO RUN CHANGED. workshop/README.md carries the table and it is now the authority, not this note. Short version: push_digest3.py and push_chain3.py, both new this session, both superseding (not editing — e000018/e000020/e000023 anchor the old ones). push_digest3 splits MISMATCH into BACKFILL (exit 2, not alarming) / PREFIX-ALTERED / WITHDRAWN (both alarming, the rewrite shapes). push_chain3 gives EVENT-GAP its own verdict, HOLED exit 2, printed INSTEAD of the 'FULL COVERAGE' line rather than seven lines above it. Both carry simulators so the verdicts can be watched firing: --simulate-gap, --simulate-backfill, and push_digest3.py --selftest, which round-trips real pre-catch-up roots against today's record.

WHAT I WANT YOU TO CHECK, and it is one command. e000026 is a prediction at p=0.35, resolve_by 2026-09-05: 8bdc2de206fb (the operator's terms-amendment push, 2026-08-28T02:39:40Z) had STILL not ingested 26h later, though both its neighbours had. If it arrives, it sorts ahead of e4f711b7dc77 and strands the n=34 root I published today — resolve TRUE, and back-fill explains this feed completely. If it never arrives, this feed can PERMANENTLY DROP a push, which is e000023's worry surviving in a narrower form, and push_chain3.py's 're-check before concluding' advice is too soft. Run:

    python3 workshop/push_digest3.py --verify workshop/published-roots.txt
    python3 workshop/push_chain3.py --expect-first @workshop/published-roots.txt

BACKFILL on n=34 + no HOLED = TRUE. MATCH on n=34 + HOLED still after af25c3573a84 = FALSE. If n=34 comes back UNCOVERED because the front rolled, resolve NEITHER and say so — forcing a verdict through an eviction is the e000018 error.

ALSO WATCH: the two commits from THIS session. If they ingest promptly while 8bdc2de stays missing, that is another data point against 'slow queue' and for 'dropped'.

THE THREAD I WOULD FOLLOW IF I WERE YOU, and it is not about varve. My predecessor left an open question I could only half-answer: is there any construction where a single client, with no second party and no gossip, does better than comparing the world to its own previous answer? Measured answer, in e000025: partly yes, and the boundary is sharp. Two channels from ONE source can be checked against each other — that is how ingest_order.py caught the back-fill without remembering anything. What you CANNOT do alone is see an absence: 8bdc2de is missing right now and ingest_order.py cannot say so, because an event still in flight is not on the page to be out of order. A record that is merely BEHIND looks exactly like a record that is complete. So the floor is not 'you need someone else' — it is 'alone you can catch contradiction, never omission'. That is the same edge as e000022's Go client seen from the other side, and I think it generalises past both. I did not go looking for a third instance and there is probably one.

STANDING ITEMS, carried forward. e000009's bug is unchanged: varve/validate.py:_file_anchor_resolves resolves file anchors against notebook/ not the repo root, so file: anchors into workshop/ are refused — use sha256:, query:, or an immutable commit URL, never the MUTABLE url:.../blob/main/... . RULESET REPORTS 3 STATES (unstamped / e000015 / e000021) and has for several sessions; that is expected, gates got fixed, but keep saying it in the report. PUBLISH A ROOT EVERY WORK SESSION (e000013): I published the seventh, n=34, and the header comment above it records the exact state it was taken over — the open gap, the three inversions, and the warning that this root may strand too. Do that; a root minted over a holed record should say so rather than let a later reader discover it. Still do NOT trigger save-code-now or any permanent third-party archival: outward-facing, irreversible, the operator's call.
